blocks.text: Get more peace of mind with the smarter, sharper wired Nest Doorbell and the intelligence of Google Home. With 2K HDR and Gemini, it provides a crisp, clear picture and more details, summarizes what happened, and lets you search video history simply by asking for something.[1,2,3]

items: Meet the wired Nest Doorbell; with 2K HDR video and Gemini, it knows what’s at your door and and what to do next (Gemini features require a Google Home premium subscription; try it for 1 month at no cost to you)[4]
No need to recharge or replace batteries; the Nest Doorbell keeps you plugged into home, day and night

The Nest Doorbell keeps your data safe with encrypted video, two-step verification, and enhanced security through your Google Account; and a green LED light lets you know when it’s processing or streaming video

With an Advanced subscription to Google Home Premium, know more about what’s happening with notifications like “Person with flowers”[3]; get even more detailed descriptions and tap to see a summary of what happened[3]

Video is crisp and clear in 2K HDR, the Nest Doorbell’s highest resolution yet[1,2]; see rich color and details, see in the dark with night vision, and see the bigger picture with an expanded 166° field of view[1]
Search your video history with help from Gemini[3]; try something like “Who let the dogs out?” to see a summary and relevant clips (subscription required)

Check in anytime with the Google Home app; see your live feed, check your video history, and talk to someone at your doorstep[5]; Google Home app and Google Account required; the Nest Doorbell (wired, 3rd gen) is not compatible with the Nest app

The Nest Doorbell sends alerts when it spots a person, package, vehicle, or animal[5]; with a Standard subscription to Google Home Premium, it can even learn the faces of your friends and family, so you know who’s at the door before they knock[5,6]
The wired Nest Doorbell’s installation requires a 16-24VAC, 10-40VA, 50/60Hz rated doorbell transformer and chime (sold separately); you may need to replace hardware
